schemaNotes.description: Shared unit schema for Iron Ridge testing eras. Combat resolution is derived, not hand-authored: look up damageTypes[attacker.damageType][defender.armorClass] to get the base effectiveness multiplier for an engagement. This naturally produces asymmetric outcomes (e.g. a tank beating rifle infantry despite its own weapon being weak against unarmored targets, because the infantry's weapon does ~none against heavy armor) without needing separate strongVs/weakVs lists per unit.
schemaNotes.resolutionModel: effectiveness = damageTypes[attackerDamageType].effectiveness[defenderArmorClass]. Apply variance range where specified before finalizing damage.

fields.name: display name
fields.unitClass: production/role category. Medieval: infantry | cavalry | artillery. WW2: infantry | vehicle | artillery.
fields.armorClass: target classification used for damage resolution: unarmored | light_armor | heavy_armor
fields.damageType: weapon family used for damage resolution: piercing | non_piercing | siege
fields.specialRules: array of short rule strings capturing mechanics not covered by the damage-type/armor-class matrix (suppression, first-strike, fortification interaction, etc.)
fields.placementCategory: automatic (standing/garrison, placed at strategic layer) | warned (range-and-time gated pre-placement) | combat_fixed (must be placed live during tactical phase, cannot reposition after) | combat_mobile (moves with field commander, placed live, repositionable)
fields.notes: free text for open design questions or balancing flags

damageTypes.description: Three-type system shared across both eras. Effectiveness is qualitative for now (high/medium/low/none); numeric multipliers TBD once point-budget/formula pass happens. 'variance' flags types where actual rolled damage should swing widely around the average rather than being a flat value.

piercing.description: Arrows/spears (medieval); autocannon rounds (WW2). Trades some stopping power against soft targets for penetration.

non_piercing.description: Swords/axes (medieval); rifle/MG small arms (WW2). Optimized against unarmored targets, minimal effect on real armor.

siege.description: Catapults (medieval, concussive-force siege engines); rockets, mortars, artillery, tank and AT-gun rounds (WW2, explosive). The only damage type that reliably threatens heavy armor and fortifications. Weak and unreliable against a single soldier, but capable of an occasional catastrophic hit.
specialRules: Only damage type effective against fortifications/structures
vs_unarmored uses a wide damage range (mostly-miss, occasional near-total-loss) rather than a flat scalar, per dispersed-target logic

units.name: Infantry
units.role: Core line troop, closes and holds ground

units.name: Archers
specialRules: First-strike: gets a ranged attack before melee units close, partially offsetting weak survivability once melee contact is made
units.notes: Weak in raw matchups by design; value comes from elevation/range positioning and first-strike damage, not a combat-line role.

units.name: Horseman (Cavalry)
units.role: Fast shock/flanking unit, punishes exposed infantry and archers
specialRules: High movement range relative to other medieval units
Speed denies archers time to loose multiple volleys before contact (mechanical advantage vs. archers, not a damage-type advantage)
Charge bonus vs. infantry may scale with distance covered before contact (future refinement)

units.name: Spearman
specialRules: Braced-formation bonus vs. cavalry charges (mechanical advantage layered on top of base damage-type resolution)

units.name: Artillery (Catapult)
units.role: Indirect siege weapon; concussive-force damage, sole unit type able to damage fortifications
specialRules: No melee capability
Can arc fire over terrain/ridgelines that block direct-fire units (per Map-01 lesson design)
Vulnerable to fast units (cavalry) closing distance due to no melee defense
units.notes: Damage type is siege/concussive, not explosive — medieval siege engines work via kinetic/concussive force rather than blast.

units.name: AT Infantry (Bazooka/Rockets)
specialRules: Low hit probability vs. unarmored/dispersed infantry regardless of raw lethality (inherits siege-type variance vs. unarmored)

units.name: Machine Gun Team
specialRules: Suppression mechanic ties into existing action-economy/exposure system
Differentiates from Rifle Infantry via suppression, not damage type (both are non_piercing)
units.notes: Crew-served weapon, loses mobility once set up — fixed counterpart to the mobile MG-nest repositioning example discussed earlier.

units.name: Mortar Team
units.role: Crew-served short/medium range indirect fire, squad-level support
specialRules: Shorter effective range than Artillery class — distinguishes it as squad-level support rather than a rolling-chassis asset
units.notes: Deliberately kept distinct from Artillery for era-symmetry — mortar is man-portable/crew-served, Artillery is vehicle-mounted.

units.name: Tank
specialRules: Beats unarmored infantry primarily via superior survivability (infantry's non_piercing weapon does ~none vs heavy_armor), not via strong offense vs unarmored (siege type is weak/variance-heavy there)
Multiple tank variants may exist with varying armor/firepower levels within this unit type — class dictates armor category, not fixed stats
Design goal: tune damage/survivability numbers so shots-to-kill vs. AT Gun is comparable in both directions despite different raw damage numbers
units.notes: Balance target: avoid tank-always-beats-AT-gun-if-both-survive-first-hit outcome. AT Gun should trade roughly evenly if it gets the engagement, offset by AT Gun's lower mobility/higher exposure as the real tradeoff, not raw combat math.

units.name: AT Gun
specialRules: Low mobility/high exposure is the intended tradeoff against Tank's mobility, not a damage-output difference
Vulnerable to being overrun by unsupported infantry assault despite strong anti-armor output
units.notes: Shares light_armor classification with LAV and Artillery. Towed/static nature may later split into its own placement rules distinct from mobile vehicles.

units.name: Light Armored Vehicle (LAV)
units.role: Fast anti-infantry/anti-light-armor vehicle; potential future mechanized-infantry transport pairing
specialRules: High mobility relative to Tank
Autocannon/small-cannon armament placed in piercing category — distinct from Tank/AT Gun's siege-type armament and from infantry's non_piercing small arms
Candidate for future mechanized-infantry pairing rule (LAV + infantry unit deployed as a combined package) rather than a separate unit type
units.notes: Shares light_armor classification with Artillery and AT Gun — distinct from Tank's heavy_armor.

units.name: Artillery (Motorized)
units.role: Long-range indirect fire, mounted on rolling chassis; sole unit type able to damage fortifications
specialRules: Longer effective range than Mortar
All variants motorized for simplicity; future refinement may split into towed/deployed vs. truck-mobile variants, affecting permanent vs. mobile deployment cost
Vulnerable to fast flanking attacks (LAV/tanks) — mirrors medieval cavalry-vs-catapult dynamic
units.notes: Deployed vs. mobile artillery distinction (towed/repositionable vs. truck-attached) flagged as future differentiation tied to deployment cost.
